name: Mỗi năm một ga
notes: chapters = seconds in film.mp4 where the film waits for a tap, taken from scene.html by stops.py: the title frame, the train standing at each year's station (PAUSE.inBeat into the year), standing at Ga Hôm Nay (PAUSE.extra), the climax (PAUSE.climax: the ticket lifted off the table), and the last frame. Each sits a quarter of a frame into its frame, so a seek shows that frame and round(t * fps) finds its boxes. hints = the scene's own words at those stops (WORDS.cue, the next button's "Xem tiếp", WORDS.hint, ui.skip); a card can override them with "chapters". reveal = null: no 3D envelope; after the last stop a tap opens the letter. slots.json: sign0 ... sign4 are the year stations' names on their hanging signs (sign), cap0-k ... cap4-k the same names over the captions (label), cap0-l ... cap5-l the captions, the last one the arrival line (caption); they fade with the scene (alpha is the 5th number of each box). board is the years on the lit board at Ga Hôm Nay (sign), ticket-names and ticket-years the names and the years printed on the ticket (text, label). Compromises: the signs and the board show their words only while the train is (nearly) standing, since a plate rushing past at hundreds of pixels a frame cannot carry painted words, and the film blurs fast frames; every year sign is as wide as the Ga Hôm Nay sign. The ticket's names and years are painted once it is lifted and straight (on the table it lies small and tilted, and the player paints only upright boxes). The board's years are dimmed as much as the veil darkens the board. photos = 5: slots.json "photos" makes the year posters on the platforms photo places, in the order the train reaches them (0 rain, 1 pines, 2 cups, 3 dinner, 4 home: the scene's stand-in drawings; on screen in frames 32-70, 81-119, 130-167, 178-216 and 227-264). Each play the player lays the card's photos (in a new order) over the posters' drawings in every frame, as each platform slides in, stands and slides away; a poster with no photo shows its drawing. A place is the poster's picture, 210 x 263 film pixels (the drawing and the light row under it; aspect 0.798, the shape the photo is cropped to), measured in render.html at each moment render.py drew; in a frame the film blurs (the average of 2, 4 or 8 moments while the train runs fast) it sits in the middle of those moments, and the photo is drawn sharp (the player paints no motion blur), so a little of the drawing's smear shows round it there. Where the window's dark edge or the curtain and its tie lie over a poster, the box is clipped to what shows of it. The film's light is laid over a photo as over the drawing: on each place, the glare on the poster's glass (white, 0.18 at the picture's top left corner, none 36% of the way along 125 degrees) and the window's warm glow along its bottom (0.07 at its bottom edge, none 28% up); on each frame's box, the window's warm 118-degree band (0.05 at its middle) and, within 80 px of the window's left or right edge, its inset shadow (its measured profile, 0.25 at the edge). The wall lamp's glow is radial and is left out (at most 5.5% over the leftmost 15 px of a leaving poster). Ga Hôm Nay, its board line (năm bên nhau) and the ticket's print are the template's own words. fonts = the faces the player paints these slots in (latin, latin-ext and vietnamese).
